messages.author: d6e672db96a0f058
messages.subject: maximum on number of nodes?
parts:
Hi All,

I'm running a a random-effects model using the nimbleMCMC function. The model works fine if the number of units in the data (the number of random effects or nodes) is of normal size (e.g. 500 units), but I get an error message if the number gets huge (e.g. 20000 units).  

Therefore, I was wondering whether there is a maximum on the number of nodes that can be specified in the model when using R-Nimble (nimbleMCMC)?   Note also that I am not monitoring these random effects.

Kind regards
Christel

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: maximum on number of nodes?
parts:
Hi Christel,

There is no built-in limit to the number of nodes.  There are practical limits, but I have seen models with nodes in your range.

Could you please send a reproducible example (or at least your model code).  If it is not something you want to share on the list, you could send it off-list.

The error message looks like one that was caused by a previously-fixed bug, so I want to be sure you are on the latest version of nimble (0.8-0).  The same message could be generated due to other problems as well.

-Perry
